title: Adaptive Witness Planner
canonical_question: Given rival cause classes, calibrated test outcomes, costs, dependencies and priors, which test should be acquired next so that the expected total cost to cause-class identifiability is minimized?
relationship_to_r4_1: R4.1 returns a minimum fixed witness set. R4.2 returns a contingent policy tree whose next test depends on earlier outcomes and stops as soon as the target cause class is identified.
bellman_recurrence: V(s)=0 when all causes in C_s share one target_class; otherwise V(s)=min_t [cost(t)+sum_o P(o|s,t)V(s_o)] over admissible tests whose dependencies are satisfied.
policy_objective: minimum expected cost to target-class identifiability
model_requirements: every decision-usable available test declares one deterministic outcome for every candidate cause
dependencies and failure domains are explicit
unavailable historical or counterfactual tests use available=false

exactness.adaptive_policy: Dynamic programming is exact under the declared deterministic outcome/prior model while resource ceilings are not exceeded.
exactness.nonadaptive_baseline: A fixed-set comparator is exhaustively enumerated under the same declared model.
exactness.resource_rule: If exact search exceeds a declared ceiling, verdict is UNKNOWN_RESOURCE_LIMIT rather than an approximate optimality claim.

benchmarks.synthetic_adaptive_advantage: t_root first; adaptive expected cost 4 versus exact fixed cost 5.
benchmarks.search_proof_adaptive: provenance_hash_audit first; adaptive expected cost 2.8 versus exact fixed cost 4.
benchmarks.palomar_xe325_adaptive: NON_IDENTIFIABLE because current soft historical evidence is not promoted into deterministic decision outcomes.

authority_ceiling: PASS establishes exact policy optimality only inside the declared planning model. Empirical outcome calibration, priors and domain failure-mode assumptions remain independently falsifiable.
next_stage_goal: Replace deterministic cause-to-outcome maps with calibrated P(outcome|cause,test), posterior updates, risk thresholds and model-uncertainty stress tests.
